","char_count":744,"fact_ids":[],"source_anchors":[{"anchor_id":"A01","source_page":"src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009"}]},{"section_id":"B","chunk_id":"B.01","merge_seq":2,"domain":null,"heading":"B — Emergency/maintenance vehicles and police stops","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## Audience and scope
This dossier supports first-time Massachusetts passenger-vehicle applicants learning emergency/maintenance vehicles and police stops. The mapped physical pages define coverage. Authored study groups are attention and preparation; moving emergency vehicles; stopped responders; traffic stops; traffic-stop conduct. Their order is a teaching choice without any claim about examination frequency. Terms, conditions, exceptions and applicant pathways stay attached to the statements that use them; no driving experience is assumed.
","char_count":550,"fact_ids":[],"source_anchors":[]},{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":3,"domain":"Emergency/maintenance vehicles and police stops","heading":"C — Emergency/maintenance vehicles and police stops","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Emergency/maintenance vehicles and police stops

FACT_ID: sec15-F01 | anchor: A01
Give driving full attention rather than being distracted by conversation, radio adjustments or eating. [A01]
Why it matters: group attention and preparation; authored recall cue full driving attention.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-F02 | anchor: A01
Look ahead and drive defensively so hazards can be seen early enough to avoid them. [A01]
Why it matters: group attention and preparation; authored recall cue look ahead for hazards.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-F03 | anchor: A01
Practice highway, nighttime and varied-weather driving and learn how to respond to emergencies such as skids and tire failures. [A01]
Why it matters: group attention and preparation; authored recall cue varied driving preparation.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-F04 | anchor: A02
Yield to an emergency vehicle using a siren, emergency flashing lights or both. [A02]
Why it matters: group moving emergency vehicles; authored recall cue emergency vehicle priority.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-F05 | anchor: A02
For an emergency vehicle approaching from any direction, pull as far right as possible and stop fully until it passes. [A02]
Why it matters: group moving emergency vehicles; authored recall cue pull right and stop.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-F06 | anchor: A02
Use mirrors and a right-turn signal to choose a safe pull-over location without moving left, braking harshly or stopping suddenly. [A02]
Why it matters: group moving emergency vehicles; authored recall cue controlled emergency pull-over.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-F07 | anchor: A02
Do not stop inside an intersection for an emergency vehicle; clear the intersection and pull over when safe. [A02]
Why it matters: group moving emergency vehicles; authored recall cue clear the intersection first.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-F08 | anchor: A02
After the emergency vehicle passes, check for additional responders and a clear lane, signal left and merge back safely. [A02]
Why it matters: group moving emergency vehicles; authored recall cue safe return after responder.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-F09 | anchor: A02
Following a responding emergency vehicle closer than three hundred feet is illegal. [A02]
Why it matters: group moving emergency vehicles; authored recall cue emergency following clearance.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-F10 | anchor: A02
Slow and stay alert near stopped fire, police, ambulance, disaster-support, highway-maintenance or recovery vehicles with flashing emergency lights. [A02]
Why it matters: group stopped responders; authored recall cue stopped responder categories.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-F11 | anchor: A02
The move-over rule requires a cautious reasonable safe speed when approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. [A02]
Why it matters: group stopped responders; authored recall cue move-over speed.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-F12 | anchor: A02
On a highway with at least four lanes including two in your direction, safely change to a lane not beside the stopped emergency vehicle. [A02]
Why it matters: group stopped responders; authored recall cue move-over lane change.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-F13 | anchor: A02
The safe move-over direction may be right or left, and if a lane change is impossible the driver must still slow and proceed cautiously. [A02]
Why it matters: group stopped responders; authored recall cue move-over alternatives.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-F14 | anchor: A02
Be ready to stop when passing an emergency vehicle and dim high beams at night. [A02]
Why it matters: group stopped responders; authored recall cue passing responder caution.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-F15 | anchor: A02
If requesting police assistance, stop in front of the cruiser rather than behind it. [A02]
Why it matters: group stopped responders; authored recall cue assistance stopping position.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-F16 | anchor: A03
Do not approach an officer handling another stopped driver; wait beside your own vehicle on the shoulder until the officer finishes. [A03]
Why it matters: group stopped responders; authored recall cue wait while officer is occupied.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec15-F17 | anchor: A03
Driving by or parking within eight hundred feet of a fire is prohibited. [A03]
Why it matters: group stopped responders; authored recall cue fire-scene clearance.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec15-F18 | anchor: A03
Do not drive across an unprotected fire hose unless a firefighter or public-safety official directs you to do so. [A03]
Why it matters: group stopped responders; authored recall cue fire hose protection.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec15-F19 | anchor: A03
A driver must pull to the roadside and stop when signaled by an officer, whether the officer is on foot or in a police vehicle. [A03]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; authored recall cue obey police stop signal.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0129]

Misconceptions: Keep each rule’s stated conditions; related requirements are not interchangeable.
Mnemonics: Authored recall cues in each block label the distinction to remember.
Glossary: Terms are explained by their source-grounded rule sentences, without added definitions.
Dynamic facts: Source edition and unresolved legal effective date require review; no current-law clearance is inferred.
","char_count":6781,"fact_ids":["sec15-F01","sec15-F02","sec15-F03","sec15-F04","sec15-F05","sec15-F06","sec15-F07","sec15-F08","sec15-F09","sec15-F10","sec15-F11","sec15-F12","sec15-F13","sec15-F14","sec15-F15","sec15-F16","sec15-F17","sec15-F18","sec15-F19"],"source_anchors":[{"anchor_id":"A01","source_page":"src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0127"},{"anchor_id":"A02","source_page":"src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0128"},{"anchor_id":"A03","source_page":"src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0129"}]},{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":4,"domain":"Emergency/maintenance vehicles and police stops","heading":"C2 — Emergency/maintenance vehicles and police stops","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Emergency/maintenance vehicles and police stops

FACT_ID: sec15-R01 | anchor: A01
Do not ignore a police stop signal or pretend not to see it. [A01]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; authored recall cue acknowledge stop signal.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec15-R02 | anchor: A01
Signal, check mirrors and move slowly and completely to the road’s right side during a police stop rather than pulling left. [A01]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; authored recall cue right-side police pull-over.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec15-R03 | anchor: A01
If the signaling officer continues past without stopping, reenter the travel lane when safe. [A01]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; authored recall cue officer continues onward.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec15-R04 | anchor: A02
Do not stop in an intersection, driveway entrance or travel lane, and follow an officer’s direction to a particular stopping place. [A02]
Why it matters: group traffic-stop conduct; authored recall cue safe police-stop location.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R05 | anchor: A02
During a stop, select Park in an automatic or neutral with the parking brake in a manual vehicle, and turn off the engine and radio. [A02]
Why it matters: group traffic-stop conduct; authored recall cue secure stopped vehicle.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R06 | anchor: A02
The driver and passengers should remain inside until the officer instructs otherwise. [A02]
Why it matters: group traffic-stop conduct; authored recall cue remain in vehicle.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R07 | anchor: A02
If directed out, stay safely away from traffic and keep hands visible. [A02]
Why it matters: group traffic-stop conduct; authored recall cue safe exit when directed.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R08 | anchor: A02
At night during a police stop, leave headlights on and turn on the interior overhead light. [A02]
Why it matters: group traffic-stop conduct; authored recall cue traffic-stop lighting.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R09 | anchor: A02
Lower the window as the officer approaches. [A02]
Why it matters: group traffic-stop conduct; authored recall cue window for communication.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R10 | anchor: A02
An officer not in uniform will show credentials, or the driver may ask to see them. [A02]
Why it matters: group traffic-stop conduct; authored recall cue officer identification.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R11 | anchor: A02
Wait for a request before reaching for license or registration and hand the documents over outside a wallet or holder. [A02]
Why it matters: group traffic-stop conduct; authored recall cue wait before retrieving documents.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R12 | anchor: A02
Keep license and registration handy while driving; a first failure to produce either document carries a thirty-five-dollar fine. [A02]
Why it matters: group traffic-stop conduct; authored recall cue produce required documents.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R13 | anchor: A02
Without the documents, the officer may request the driver’s name and address and the owner’s name and address when different. [A02]
Why it matters: group traffic-stop conduct; authored recall cue identity information request.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R14 | anchor: A02
Failure to comply with the identity request or giving a false name or address can bring a one-hundred-dollar fine, and refusal may lead to arrest and criminal charges. [A02]
Why it matters: group traffic-stop conduct; authored recall cue identity refusal consequences.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R15 | anchor: A02
A Massachusetts registration identifies the insurer and explains that Massachusetts does not issue an insurance card, while other jurisdictions may request insurance proof under their laws. [A02]
Why it matters: group traffic-stop conduct; authored recall cue insurance document difference.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R16 | anchor: A02
Keep both the driver’s and passengers’ hands plainly visible. [A02]
Why it matters: group traffic-stop conduct; authored recall cue visible hands.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R17 | anchor: A02
Give the officer full attention without using a cell phone during the stop. [A02]
Why it matters: group traffic-stop conduct; authored recall cue attention during stop.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R18 | anchor: A02
Avoid sudden movements or reaching into hidden areas, and make sure passengers avoid those movements too. [A02]
Why it matters: group traffic-stop conduct; authored recall cue avoid unexpected reaching.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R19 | anchor: A02
Remain in the vehicle when the officer goes back to the cruiser. [A02]
Why it matters: group traffic-stop conduct; authored recall cue wait in vehicle.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ma-d:massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]
